title: Computer names, duplicate records, the ssh noticer and remote setup rows
owns: app/main/targets/registry.ts, the record/naming/offer parts of app/main/targets/runtime.ts, the ssh noticer, app/main/targets/setup-check.ts

findings.title: A computer added by its full name can't be addressed by its short name ('on build-01'): the task runs here, or the model hits a dead end
findings.area: Naming a computer in a request / SSH
findings.scenario: The settings placeholder's own example is 'deploy@build-01.example.com'. Ember labels that host 'build-01.example.com', and its only names are the id, the dest's host part and the resolved hostname, each matched as a whole run of words. The user says or types 'on build-01, check the disk' with this computer picked. With no model target the task binds to this computer, so df -h runs here and the answer describes the wrong machine. If the model passes target 'build-01', bind() says 'Ember isn't set up to work on that computer yet… (offer_connect)', and offer_connect('build-01') answers 'Ember doesn't know a computer called build-01. Tell the user to add it in Ember's settings (Computers).' That is a computer already listed there. If the model uses the FQDN it saw in list_computers, bind() refuses it with 'The user didn't name that computer'. Only saying the whole FQDN works.
findings.evidence: Ran buildTargets with host id 'build-01.example.com' (connected) and the picker on 'local': bind({userWords:'on build-01, check the disk'}) gave id 'local'; with choice 'build-01' it gave the 'isn't set up' refusal; with choice 'build-01.example.com' it gave 'The user didn't name that computer'; offerConnect('build-01', words) gave 'Ember doesn't know a computer called build-01…'. resolve.ts bindTarget on the registry's names gave the same results.
findings.fix: Add the first DNS label of the host id, dest host part and resolved hostname as an extra name for each SSH entry when it is unique among hosts and at least MIN_NAME long. Use the same alias list in offerConnect's lookup (runtime.ts:1375). When two hosts share a short name, keep today's TWO_NAMED question.

findings.title: A WSL distro with a versioned name ('Ubuntu-22.04', 'kali-linux') isn't named by 'in Ubuntu': the task silently runs on Windows and the wrong-target guard stays quiet
findings.area: Naming a computer / WSL distro picking
findings.scenario: A distro installed from the Store is called 'Ubuntu-22.04' or 'Ubuntu-24.04', and others are 'kali-linux' or 'openSUSE-Leap-15.5'. A distro's names are its exact name, '<name> (WSL)' and, for the default distro only, WSL/Linux. The docs' example, 'in Ubuntu, list my home folder', names nothing. With no model target the task binds to this PC and runs on Windows. 'in Ubuntu, delete build/' is the worst case: otherTargetsNamed and placesNamed find nothing ('Ubuntu' has no dot, hyphen or digit), so the delete is announced and run on Windows as 'asked'. If the model passes target 'Ubuntu', the user is sent to 'add it in Ember's settings (Computers)' as an SSH host.
findings.evidence: resolve.ts targetsNamed with names ['Ubuntu-22.04','Ubuntu-22.04 (WSL)','WSL','Linux','Linux side']: 'in Ubuntu, list my home folder' gave [] and bindTarget gave local; 'in Ubuntu 22.04…' and 'in WSL…' gave the distro. Through the runtime rig (win32, WSL on, distro 'Ubuntu-22.04'): bind(no choice) gave local; bind(choice 'Ubuntu') gave the 'isn't set up…offer_connect' refusal; offerConnect('Ubuntu') gave 'Ember doesn't know a computer called Ubuntu. Tell the user to add it in Ember's settings (Computers).'; agent.othersNamed('local','in Ubuntu, delete build/') gave [].
findings.fix: Give each distro an extra name for its leading word(s) before the first '-', '_' or digit ('Ubuntu', 'kali', 'openSUSE') when unique among distros. Also let otherTargetsNamed count that name, so a destructive request that names it always asks. If the words only partly match one distro, refuse with 'Did you mean Ubuntu-22.04 (WSL)?'.

findings.title: The same computer added under two spellings creates two records, a second consent card, a repeated 'Bring Ember' offer and a connection that can fight the first for the remote's lock
findings.area: Adding a computer / Bring Ember offer
findings.scenario: The user adds 'build-01' (an alias) in settings and connects. They later run 'ssh deploy@build-01' in a terminal. The noticer compares dest strings only, so it offers 'You're connected to build-01. Bring Ember there too?' although Ember is already connected. Clicking Bring Ember creates 'build-01-2' (same deploy@build-01.example.com) with its own card and connection. Settings then lists two identical rows. The remote helper allows one agent per PC and user: the second agent waits the grace plus 3 s, then SIGTERMs the first. The first then shows 'Lost build-01' and starts its own reconnect loop, which does the same to the second, so they can alternate every 20 to 25 s. The same dedupe gap makes 'on build-01.example.com' match both hosts, and Ember then asks 'which one'.
findings.evidence: Rig: host {id:'build-01', dest:'build-01'} connected; act add 'deploy@build-01' gave ok and settings.hosts [build-01:build-01:deploy@build-01.example.com, build-01-2:deploy@build-01:deploy@build-01.example.com], with a second consent card 'Bring Ember to build-01-2?'. Noticer with seen dest 'deploy@build-01' while 'build-01' is connected still showed the bubble 'You're connected to build-01'. sameDest (runtime.ts:193) compares h.dest and port only, and is used at lines 791 and 1039. app/remote/lock.ts:80-100 shows the same-pcId wait then SIGTERM takeover.
findings.fix: Dedupe on the resolved identity (user, hostname, port, jump list) from ssh -G, not on the typed string. In addAndConnect, reuse the matching record and connect it. In the noticer's connected() and dismissed(), compare resolved identities too. Tell the user 'already added as build-01'.

findings.title: A stopped WSL distro is announced as 'not connected' in the handle badge and its accessible name
findings.scenario: The user picks 'Ubuntu (WSL)' in Work on while it's stopped (distros stop when idle). The handle shows a grey dot and the tooltip/aria-label 'Working on Ubuntu (WSL) (not connected)'. A distro isn't connected to anything and starts on the first command.
findings.evidence: registry.ts gives state 'off' for a distro that isn't running; targetBadge returned label 'Working on Ubuntu (WSL) (not connected)' for it (run against the real functions).
findings.fix: For kind 'wsl' and state 'off' say '(stopped)' or nothing, and use a neutral dot. Keep 'not connected' for SSH.

findings.title: The 'Ember can work in WSL' offer only appears after the user names WSL in a request while it's off; the docs say 'when Ember first sees WSL'
findings.scenario: A Windows user with WSL installed who never says 'in WSL' is never offered WSL: the only path is settings › Computers. The offer then also needs the model to pass a target or the user's words to contain 'WSL' (not 'Linux').
findings.evidence: offerWsl() has one caller, inside bind(), behind targetsNamed(words, 'WSL'). docs/COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md:271 says 'When Ember first sees WSL it offers…'; CHANGELOG repeats that WSL is off until turned on.
findings.fix: Either offer once when discovery first finds a usable distro (after onboarding, at most once, with 'Not now' sticking), or change the docs to say it is offered after you ask for WSL.

findings.title: Backticked commands show their backticks in plain-text bubbles and settings messages; a failed reconnect on an unknown host key says 'sign in again'
findings.scenario: The key-changed fix reads 'remove the old key in a terminal with `ssh-keygen -R build-01`', and the OpenSSH-missing message 'Install OpenSSH (Linux: `sudo dnf install openssh-clients`; Windows: …)', with literal backticks, because the bubble and the settings line use textContent. Also the reconnect handler treats unknown-host-key as 'sign in again' (runtime.ts:1098), though no sign-in is needed.
findings.evidence: Rendered the overlay with the message text: backticks are visible. bubble.ts setThought uses textContent. MESSAGES.* contain backticks; p.kind === 'unknown-host-key' maps to signInAgain().
findings.fix: Drop the backticks, or render code spans in these two surfaces. Word the reconnect needing a host key as 'build-01 needs you to check its key again' with Reconnect.

findings.title: A known host that isn't connected tells the model 'Connect it from Ember's menu first' and never mentions offer_connect
findings.scenario: 'on build-01, check the disk' with build-01 added but disconnected binds to it, and handsFor refuses with that sentence. A model that follows it tells the user to use the menu (Work on › build-01), when offer_connect would put a Connect button right in the bubble, as it does for unknown hosts.
findings.evidence: registry.ts:178 and runtime.ts:1189 produce the text; offerConnect() handles a known, disconnected host correctly (rig: it shows the 'Connect to build-01?' bubble).
findings.fix: Make the refusal say 'Call offer_connect so the user can click Connect' (the lost case: 'Reconnect it from the bubble or Settings', since the menu item is disabled while lost).

findings.title: The 'offer to bring Ember along when I run ssh' scan is on by default for everyone, including existing users who never accepted a card, against 'off until you turn them on'
findings.scenario: After upgrading, an existing user who never touched SSH has Ember poll the window title every 2 s. When a terminal's title changes it reads the process list for `ssh` command lines (Linux /proc, macOS ps, a hidden PowerShell CIM query on Windows, and per running WSL distro). It can pop 'You're connected to X — Bring Ember there too?'. The docs open with 'All three are off until you turn them on… nothing new happens until they accept a card', and the first-run text is unchanged (CONSENT_VERSION 1).
findings.evidence: `offerSsh: z.boolean().default(true)` (settings.ts:120); the noticer is enabled by `sshAllowed(admin()) && settings.get().targets.offerSsh` (runtime.ts:1025) with no host record or card required. computers-copy.ts shows the switch checked unless it is explicitly false. §4.1 describes the behaviour but the intro and CHANGELOG do not.
findings.fix: Default offerSsh to false until the user has added a computer or accepted one SSH card (or ask once with the offer itself). Otherwise state it plainly in the intro, README and CHANGELOG as the one default-on behaviour.

findings.title: The ssh noticer offers 'Bring Ember there' for non-interactive ssh such as git over ssh, scp and rsync
findings.scenario: A developer pulls from GitHub over ssh (`git fetch`, an IDE's auto-fetch) or runs scp/rsync while their terminal's title changes. Ember offers 'You're connected to github.com — Bring Ember there too?', and Bring Ember then connects to GitHub's ssh server.
findings.evidence: sshDestination stops at the first word after the destination ('the first other word after it starts the command') but still returns the destination. It returns {dest:'git@github.com'} for `ssh git@github.com git-upload-pack 'o/r.git'`, {dest:'build-01'} for `ssh -x -oForwardAgent=no … -- build-01 scp -t /tmp`, and {dest:'devbox'} for `ssh -T -D 1080 devbox bash`.
findings.fix: Return null when words follow the destination (a remote command is present). Optionally also skip -T, -D and other non-interactive shapes and well-known git hosts.

findings.title: Setup-check rows for other computers: double full stop, stray backticks, Windows and Linux instructions together, wrong version
findings.scenario: The row for a Mac remote reads '…is on.. System Settings › General › Sharing…' (doctor.ts:101 already ends in a full stop and setup-check.ts appends '. ' + fix). On Linux, a missing ssh shows 'No SSH client found. Ember can't find SSH on this computer. Install OpenSSH (Linux: `sudo dnf install openssh-clients`; Windows: Settings › Apps › Optional features…)', which repeats itself, shows literal backticks (the page sets textContent) and tells a Linux user about Windows. 'Command window terminal' shows 'Install util-linux (`sudo dnf install util-linux`)' the same way, even on macOS. An OpenSSH 8.2 Windows PC gets 'Passwords can't be asked here… Ember needs OpenSSH 8.1 or newer', which is already satisfied.
findings.evidence: Strings produced by setupChecks() over sshClientRow, commandTerminalRow, remoteTccRow and powershellRow: gen.json in the scratch folder. Sources: doctor.ts:40-42, 53-58, 101.
findings.fix: Join with a full stop only when detail doesn't already end with one. Pick the OS-specific install line for the OS in use. Remove backticks, or render `code` segments. Give the 8.1 to 8.3 case its own text ('needs OpenSSH 8.4 or newer for passwords'). Don't print the redundant 'Ember can't find SSH' sentence.

findings.title: Setup-check rows for SSH and Mac remotes contain a double full stop, a repeated sentence, wrong version advice and literal backticks
findings.scenario: setupChecks joins detail and fix as `${detail}. ${fix}` without checking punctuation. A Mac remote's row reads "…until \"Allow full disk access for remote users\" is on.. System Settings › General › Sharing › Remote Login › ⓘ › Allow full disk access for remote users." (double full stop, straight quotes where the consent card uses curly, and a fix that is a menu path, not a sentence). With no SSH client it reads "No SSH client found. Ember can't find SSH on this computer. Install OpenSSH (Linux: `sudo dnf install openssh-clients`; …)" (the same fact twice, with Markdown backticks shown literally). For a Windows client 8.1 to 8.3 it reads "Passwords can't be asked here: keys and the ssh-agent only. Ember needs OpenSSH 8.1 or newer: update…", which tells someone who has 8.1 that they need 8.1.
findings.evidence: Ran setupChecks over sshClientRow, remoteTccRow, commandTerminalRow and powershellRow: the outputs are exactly the strings above (probe3). targets/doctor.ts:58 pairs the "Passwords can't be asked here" detail with OLD_SSH_WIN_FIX (line 42, "8.1 or newer"), while the real requirement for passwords is 8.4 (prompt/copy.ts, COMMANDS doc §4.6). doctor.ts:101-102 holds the straight-quote and period-plus-period text; line 40 holds the repeated sentence.
findings.fix: Join with a check for a trailing full stop (`/[.!?]$/.test(detail) ? " " : ". "`), use curly quotes at doctor.ts:101, write the Mac fix as a sentence ("Turn it on in System Settings › General › Sharing › Remote Login › ⓘ."), shorten the no-client detail to "No SSH client found" plus the install sentence, strip or style backticks for the window, and give the 8.1-8.3 case its own fix ("Update the OpenSSH Client to 8.4 or newer to enter passwords in Ember").
